column2: Objects, arrows between them, a way to compose arrows that meet end to start, and an identity arrow on each object, obeying the identity and associativity laws.

column1: What does \( g \circ f \) mean, and which runs first?
column2: g after f: \( (g \circ f)(x) = g(f(x)) \). f runs first. It needs f to end where g starts.
Identity: \( f \circ \mathrm{id}_A = f = \mathrm{id}_B \circ f \). Associativity: \( h \circ (g \circ f) = (h \circ g) \circ f \).
Objects are sets, arrows are functions, composition is function composition, and identities send each element to itself.

column1: How is a Unix pipe a composition?
column2: Each command is an arrow on byte streams. \( a | b | c \) is \( c \circ b \circ a \). cat with no file acts as the identity.

column1: When is \( f : A \to B \) an isomorphism?
column2: When some \( g : B \to A \) has \( g \circ f = \mathrm{id}_A \) and \( f \circ g = \mathrm{id}_B \). In Set, exactly the bijections.
A map between categories sending objects to objects and arrows to arrows, with \( F(\mathrm{id}) = \mathrm{id} \) and \( F(g \circ f) = F(g) \circ F(f) \). Example: T to []T, f to Map(·, f).

column1: What is a natural transformation \( \alpha : F \Rightarrow G \)?
column2: One arrow \( \alpha_T : F(T) \to G(T) \) per object, with \( G(f) \circ \alpha_A = \alpha_B \circ F(f) \) for every \( f : A \to B \). Example: First from []T to Option[T].

column1: What does it mean for a diagram to commute?
column2: Every two paths between the same pair of objects compose to the same arrow.

column1: State the universal property of the product \( A \times B \).
column2: For any \( f : X \to A \) and \( g : X \to B \) there is exactly one \( \langle f, g \rangle : X \to A \times B \) with \( \pi_1 \circ \langle f, g \rangle = f \) and \( \pi_2 \circ \langle f, g \rangle = g \).

column1: What is a coproduct in Set and in Go?
column2: The disjoint union \( A + B \), with \( |A + B| = |A| + |B| \). In Go: a tagged union, an interface with a type switch, or (value, error) by convention.

column1: Terminal and initial objects in Set?
column2: Terminal: any one-element set, one arrow in from everything. Initial: the empty set, one arrow (the empty function) out to everything.

column1: What does currying say in category terms?
column2: Arrows \( A \times B \to C \) match arrows \( A \to C^B \) one to one. Counting: \( |C|^{|A||B|} = (|C|^{|B|})^{|A|} \).

column1: What are the parts of a monad?
column2: A functor M, a unit \( A \to M(A) \) such as Some(v) or (v, nil), and a bind that chains steps \( A \to M(B) \), obeying left identity, right identity and associativity.

column1: Why does a generic Go func with a type switch risk failing naturality?
column2: It can act differently for one type. Then converting before applying differs from applying before converting. Parametricity holds only when code never inspects types.
